components.name: accessEditor
components.title: Access Editor
components.summary: An owner and admin editor for who may open the app: access mode, users, admins and a summary of unsaved changes.

params.type: {owner: string, draft: {users: string[], admins: string[], mode: "list"|"org"}, base?: {users: string[], admins: string[], mode: "list"|"org"}|null, canEditUsers?: boolean, canEditAdmins?: boolean, canEditMode?: boolean, input?: {users?: string, admins?: string}, messages?: {users?: string|null, admins?: string|null, mode?: string|null}, id?: string}
params.name: p
description: `draft` is the working copy; `base` is the saved copy and turns on the New marks and the change summary. `canEditUsers` defaults to true; admins and mode are owner-only and default to false.

The view renders no form, so Enter in an Add input does nothing by itself: the app should delegate a keydown on Enter from [data-act="accessEditor:input"] to the same handler as accessEditor:add for that data-list.

emits: accessEditor:mode (data-mode)
accessEditor:add (data-list)
accessEditor:remove (data-list, data-email)
accessEditor:input (data-list; read the value)
components.a11y: The mode is a radio group in a fieldset with a legend. Each list is a section with a heading and a list; Remove buttons say who and from which list. The owner row says "Owner" and "Cannot be removed" in words. New and Other domain are text tags, not colour alone. Errors are role=alert and linked to the input with aria-describedby.

examples.code: accessEditor({ owner: "owner@example.org", draft: { users: ["owner@example.org", "ana@example.org"], admins: [], mode: "list" }, canEditUsers: true })

accessEditor({ owner: "owner@example.org", draft: { users: ["owner@example.org", "ana@example.org"], admins: ["bo@example.org"], mode: "list" }, canEditUsers: true, canEditAdmins: true, canEditMode: true })
accessEditor({ owner: "owner@example.org", draft: { users: ["owner@example.org"], admins: [], mode: "org" }, canEditUsers: true, canEditMode: true })

accessEditor({ owner: "owner@example.org", draft: { users: ["owner@example.org", "ana@example.org", "guest@other.test"], admins: [], mode: "list" }, base: { users: ["owner@example.org", "cy@example.org"], admins: [], mode: "list" }, canEditUsers: true })

accessEditor({ owner: "owner@example.org", draft: { users: ["owner@example.org"], admins: [], mode: "list" }, canEditUsers: true, input: { users: "not-an-email" }, messages: { users: "not-an-email is not a valid email address" } })

components.name: accordion
components.title: Accordion
components.summary: A stack of native disclosures; single mode opens one at a time, multiple lets any number stay open.

params.type: {items: Array<{value: string, title: string, content?: unknown, open?: boolean}>, type?: "single"|"multiple", k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `type` is "single" (default: items share a name attribute, so the browser closes the others) or "multiple" (no name). `content` is SafeHtml or text. `open` opens an item at render; in single mode only the first open item is honoured. `k` prefixes the shared name and each summary's data-k ("<k>-<value>", default "acc"; give every accordion on a page its own). The open state lives in the browser, so re-rendering the accordion resets it to the `open` props: keep it out of regions that redraw often, or pass the state back in.

components.a11y: Native details and summary: Enter and Space toggle, the summary is focusable and announced as expanded or collapsed with no ARIA. The chevron is a drawn shape that turns when open, so the state is not colour alone. Motion: where the browser supports ::details-content and interpolate-size the panel animates its height over --dur-3 times --motion-scale (zero under reduced motion); elsewhere it snaps.

examples.code: accordion({ k: "faq", items: [{ value: "a", title: "Is it accessible?", content: "Yes. It uses native disclosure." }, { value: "b", title: "Is it styled?", content: "Yes, with kit tokens." }, { value: "c", title: "Is it animated?", content: "Where the browser can." }] })
accordion({ k: "faq-m", type: "multiple", items: [{ value: "a", title: "Shipping", content: "Ships from Acme in two days." }, { value: "b", title: "Returns", content: "Thirty day returns." }] })
accordion({ k: "faq-o", items: [{ value: "a", title: "Is it accessible?", content: "Yes.", open: true }, { value: "b", title: "Is it styled?", content: "Yes." }] })
accordion({ k: "faq-e", items: [] })

components.name: alert
components.title: Alert
components.summary: An inline message with an icon, a title and a description, default or destructive.

params.type: {title?: string, description?: unknown, variant?: "default"|"destructive", live?: "alert"|"status"|"none", k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `description` takes SafeHtml or text. `variant` destructive swaps the info icon for a warning triangle and tints the text and the border. `live` sets the role: "alert" (assertive, the default for destructive), "status" (polite, the default for default) or "none" for static text that must not be announced.

components.a11y: role="alert" or role="status" (or none), so a message inserted by a re-render is announced. The two variants differ by icon shape and the title text as well as colour; the icon is aria-hidden.

examples.code: alert({ title: "Heads up", description: "Your changes are saved as a draft." })
alert({ title: "Could not save", description: "The server refused the change. Try again.", variant: "destructive" })

components.name: appShell
components.title: App Shell
components.summary: The app frame: a sidebar and, beside it, a site header (sidebar trigger, divider, breadcrumb or page title, right-aligned actions) over the page content.

params.type: {sidebar: any, title: string, breadcrumb?: Array<{label?: string, href?: string, ellipsis?: boolean}>, actions?: unknown, content?: unknown, variant?: "sidebar"|"floating"|"inset", k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `sidebar` takes the props of the `sidebar` view (an `id` is required; the trigger finds the sidebar by it). `title` is the page title: the visible h1, or, when `breadcrumb` items are given, a screen-reader-only h1 beside the visible trail (the last item is the current page). `actions` is SafeHtml for the right of the header (typically ghost or outline buttons). `content` is the page, padded 16px (24px from 768px wide) and built by the app, for example with `dashboard` or `settingsLayout`. `variant` sets the sidebar and layout variant together (default: the sidebar's own, else "sidebar"); "inset" draws the page as a rounded card on the sidebar colour. `k` prefixes the trigger's data-k (default "<sidebar id>-trigger"). Mount the `sidebar` island (sidebarIsland) after every render; the trigger and Ctrl or Cmd plus B need it. Needs sidebar.css, sheet.css and button.css.

emits: sidebar:toggle (the trigger; the island handles it)
plus the acts of the sidebar items and of `actions`
components.a11y: The inset is a main landmark labelled "Content" and the sidebar a labelled nav. The page always has one h1. The trigger is a button with an sr-only name, aria-controls and aria-expanded, and it shows its name as a tip. The header row is a plain div, so the page keeps a single banner.

examples.code: appShell({ title: "Overview", sidebar: { id: "shell-a", shortcut: false, header: "Acme", groups: [{ label: "Registry", items: [{ label: "Overview", href: "#overview", icon: "home", active: true }, { label: "Reports", href: "#reports", icon: "chart" }] }] }, content: "Page content." })

appShell({ title: "Billing", breadcrumb: [{ label: "Settings", href: "#settings" }, { label: "Billing" }], sidebar: { id: "shell-b", shortcut: false, groups: [{ items: [{ label: "Settings", href: "#settings", icon: "settings", active: true }] }] }, content: "Invoices for Acme." })

appShell({ title: "Documents", actions: "Share", sidebar: { id: "shell-c", shortcut: false, groups: [{ items: [{ label: "Documents", href: "#docs", icon: "file", active: true }] }] }, content: "No documents yet." })

appShell({ title: "Overview", variant: "inset", sidebar: { id: "shell-d", shortcut: false, header: "Acme", groups: [{ items: [{ label: "Overview", href: "#overview", icon: "home", active: true }] }] }, content: "Page content." })

components.name: areaChart
components.title: Area Chart
components.summary: An SVG area chart over a row per category: one or more series, stacked or 100 percent stacked, with optional gradient and pattern fills.

params.type: {title?: string, data: Array<Record<string, unknown>>, xKey: string, series: Array<{key: string, label?: string, color?: string, pattern?: "none"|"stripes"|"dots"}>, curve?: "natural"|"linear"|"step"|"monotone", stacked?: boolean, expand?: boolean, gradient?: boolean, legend?: boolean, grid?: boolean, axes?: boolean|{x?: boolean, y?: boolean}, height?: number, width?: number, k?: string, enter?: boolean, emptyText?: string, valueFormat?: ((v: number) => string)|"number"|"percent"|"compact", xFormat?: ((v: unknown) => string)|"number"|"percent"|"compact"}
params.name: p
description: `series[].color` is `chart-1` to `chart-6` or another token name (default: the next chart colour). `stacked` stacks the series, `expand` stacks them to 100 percent. `gradient` fades each fill from .8 to .1 opacity. `axes` shows the x labels by default and the y labels when `{y: true}`. `k` namespaces the ids and keys when several charts share a page. `enter` adds `data-enter` so the lines draw and the areas fade in (set it only when the data is new). Wrap it in a card: `card({ title, description, content: areaChart(...), footer })`; the chart is `height` px tall (default 250) and `width` units wide (default 600), full width of its container. Mount `chartFitIsland` for a full-width chart: it redraws at the measured width so the text stays 12px. A function `valueFormat` or `xFormat` cannot travel as data, so such a chart keeps the static width; use the names "number", "percent" or "compact" to keep it fit.

components.a11y: Apps mount chartFitIsland for a full-width chart; without it the chart still works at its fixed height. The svg is an image named by `title`; every category is one focusable group (tab stop) whose tip and label read all series ("Jan: Desktop 186, Mobile 80"). A sr-only table after the svg lists the same data. With more than one series the legend is always shown and `pattern` gives each series a texture, so colour is never the only signal.

examples.code: areaChart({ title: "Visitors", data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237 }, { m: "Apr", d: 73 }, { m: "May", d: 209 }, { m: "Jun", d: 214 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop", color: "chart-1" }], k: "area-a" })
areaChart({ title: "Visitors", curve: "linear", data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }], k: "area-b" })

areaChart({ title: "Visitors", curve: "step", data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237 }, { m: "Apr", d: 73 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }], k: "area-c" })

areaChart({ title: "Visitors by device", stacked: true, data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186, mo: 80 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305, mo: 200 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237, mo: 120 }, { m: "Apr", d: 73, mo: 190 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop", color: "chart-1" }, { key: "mo", label: "Mobile", color: "chart-2" }], k: "area-d", enter: true })

areaChart({ title: "Share of visitors", expand: true, axes: { x: true, y: true }, data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186, mo: 80, t: 20 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305, mo: 200, t: 40 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237, mo: 120, t: 60 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop", color: "chart-1" }, { key: "mo", label: "Mobile", color: "chart-2" }, { key: "t", label: "Tablet", color: "chart-3" }], k: "area-e" })

areaChart({ title: "Visitors", gradient: true, data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186, mo: 80 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305, mo: 200 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237, mo: 120 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop", color: "chart-1" }, { key: "mo", label: "Mobile", color: "chart-2" }], k: "area-f" })
areaChart({ title: "Visitors", legend: true, data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }], k: "area-g" })

areaChart({ title: "Visitors by device", data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186, mo: 80 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305, mo: 200 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237, mo: 120 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop", pattern: "stripes" }, { key: "mo", label: "Mobile", pattern: "dots" }], k: "area-h" })
areaChart({ title: "Visitors", data: [], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }] })

components.name: avatar
components.title: Avatar
components.summary: A round picture of a person or account, with initials when there is no picture.

params.type: {name: string, src?: string, size?: "sm"|"default"|"lg", k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `name` is required: it is the accessible name and the source of the initials (first and last word, at most two letters; "?" when empty). `src` is an https image URL; anything else (http, relative, data: or an unsafe scheme) is ignored and the initials show. The image is requested with referrerpolicy="no-referrer". The image sits over the initials with empty alt text, so a picture that fails to load leaves the initials visible. Pass `src` in an app to show a picture, for example avatar({ name: "Ada Lovelace", src: user.photoUrl }); the examples omit it so the gallery makes no image request. Sizes are 24, 32 and 40px.

components.a11y: The wrapper is role="img" with the name as aria-label, and both the initials and the picture are hidden from assistive tech, so the person is announced once by name.

examples.code: avatar({ name: "Ada Lovelace" })
avatar({ name: "Acme Support", size: "sm" })
avatar({ name: "Grace", size: "lg" })

components.name: badge
components.title: Badge
components.summary: A small pill label, with status variants that carry a word and a shape.

params.type: {text?: string, variant?: "default"|"secondary"|"outline"|"destructive"|"ok"|"warn"|"bad"|"info", tip?: string, k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `text` is the label. The status variants ok, warn, bad and info show a leading shape (circle, triangle, square, diamond) before the text, and without `text` they show a default word (OK, Warning, Problem, Info), so status is never colour alone. Unknown variants fall back to default.

components.a11y: Plain text in a span. The status shape is aria-hidden and the word carries the meaning. A tip is `data-tip` with the same text as sr-only text in the badge.

examples.code: badge({ text: "Beta" })
badge({ text: "Draft", variant: "secondary" })
badge({ text: "v1.2", variant: "outline" })
badge({ text: "Removed", variant: "destructive" })
badge({ variant: "ok" })
badge({ text: "Review due", variant: "warn", tip: "Due in 3 days" })
badge({ text: "Overdue", variant: "bad" })
badge({ variant: "info" })

components.name: bandBar
components.title: Band Bar
components.summary: A horizontal bar of ranges or thresholds with an optional value marker and a key.

params.type: {min?: number, max?: number, bands?: Band[], value?: number|null, unit?: string, label?: string, emptyText?: string}
params.name: p
description: `bands` are `{from, to, label?, status?}` on one scale (`min` and `max` default to the bands' extent); `value` puts a marker on the scale; `unit` is appended to ranges and the value ("%" directly, any other unit after a space). No usable bands gives the empty state with `emptyText` (default "No data").

components.a11y: The bar is one image whose label states the value, its band and every band range; the drawn bands are aria-hidden and carry the same figures as a tip. A visible key repeats each band name and range, so status is text, and every status except ok has its own fill pattern. A value in a gap between bands is stated as outside the bands, and one beyond the scale as above or below it with its real figure; the value is also printed under the bar for sighted users. The empty state is announced once (its visible text is aria-hidden).

examples.code: bandBar({ label: "Patch age", unit: "days", bands: [{ from: 0, to: 30, label: "Fresh", status: "ok" }, { from: 30, to: 90, label: "Ageing", status: "warn" }, { from: 90, to: 365, label: "Stale", status: "bad" }] })
bandBar({ label: "Coverage", unit: "%", min: 0, max: 100, value: 72, bands: [{ from: 0, to: 50, status: "bad" }, { from: 50, to: 80, status: "warn" }, { from: 80, to: 100, status: "ok" }] })
bandBar({ bands: [] })

components.name: barChart
components.title: Bar Chart
components.summary: An SVG bar chart: vertical or horizontal, one series or several (grouped or stacked), with value labels, negative values, an active bar and per-row colours.

params.type: {title?: string, data: Array<Record<string, unknown>>, xKey: string, series: Array<{key: string, label?: string, color?: string, pattern?: "none"|"stripes"|"dots"}>, orientation?: "vertical"|"horizontal", stacked?: boolean, labels?: boolean, negative?: boolean, activeIndex?: number, colorKey?: string, radius?: number, legend?: boolean, grid?: boolean, axes?: boolean|{x?: boolean, y?: boolean}, height?: number, width?: number, k?: string, enter?: boolean, emptyText?: string, valueFormat?: ((v: number) => string)|"number"|"percent"|"compact", xFormat?: ((v: unknown) => string)|"number"|"percent"|"compact"}
params.name: p
description: Several series are grouped side by side; `stacked` stacks them. `labels` writes the value at the end of each bar (not on stacks). `negative` colours values below zero with `chart-2` (a single series). `activeIndex` draws that row's bar at .8 opacity with a dashed outline. `colorKey` names a row field holding `chart-1` to `chart-6` (or a token name) for a colour per row (a single series). `radius` overrides the corner radius (default 8 single, 5 horizontal, 4 grouped or stacked). `k` namespaces ids and keys; `enter` makes the bars grow in. Wrap it in a card: `card({ title, description, content: barChart(...), footer })`. The chart is `height` px tall (default 250) and `width` units wide (default 600), full width of its container. Mount `chartFitIsland` for a full-width chart: it redraws at the measured width so the text stays 12px. A function `valueFormat` or `xFormat` cannot travel as data, so such a chart keeps the static width; use the names "number", "percent" or "compact" to keep it fit.

components.a11y: Apps mount chartFitIsland for a full-width chart; without it the chart still works at its fixed height. The svg is an image named by `title`; every category is one focusable group (tab stop) whose tip and label read all series ("Jan: Desktop 186, Mobile 80"). A sr-only table after the svg lists the same data. With more than one series the legend is always shown and `pattern` textures the bars, so colour is never the only signal; negative bars sit below the baseline.

examples.code: barChart({ title: "Visitors", data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237 }, { m: "Apr", d: 73 }, { m: "May", d: 209 }, { m: "Jun", d: 214 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }], k: "bar-a", enter: true })
barChart({ title: "Visitors", orientation: "horizontal", data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }], k: "bar-b" })

barChart({ title: "Visitors by device", data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186, mo: 80 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305, mo: 200 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237, mo: 120 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop", color: "chart-1" }, { key: "mo", label: "Mobile", color: "chart-2", pattern: "stripes" }], k: "bar-c" })

barChart({ title: "Visitors by device", stacked: true, data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186, mo: 80 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305, mo: 200 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237, mo: 120 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop", color: "chart-1" }, { key: "mo", label: "Mobile", color: "chart-2", pattern: "dots" }], k: "bar-d" })
barChart({ title: "Visitors", labels: true, data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }], k: "bar-e" })

barChart({ title: "Net change", negative: true, data: [{ m: "Jan", v: 186 }, { m: "Feb", v: -205 }, { m: "Mar", v: -207 }, { m: "Apr", v: 173 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "v", label: "Change" }], k: "bar-f" })
barChart({ title: "Visitors", activeIndex: 2, data: [{ m: "Jan", d: 186 }, { m: "Feb", d: 305 }, { m: "Mar", d: 237 }], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }], k: "bar-g" })

barChart({ title: "Browsers", colorKey: "fill", data: [{ b: "Chrome", n: 275, fill: "chart-1" }, { b: "Safari", n: 200, fill: "chart-2" }, { b: "Firefox", n: 187, fill: "chart-3" }], xKey: "b", series: [{ key: "n", label: "Visitors" }], k: "bar-h" })
barChart({ title: "Visitors", data: [], xKey: "m", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop" }] })

components.name: breadcrumb
components.title: Breadcrumb
components.summary: A trail of links to the current page, with an optional ellipsis for collapsed levels.

params.type: {items: {label?: string, href?: string, ellipsis?: boolean}[], ariaLabel?: string, k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `items` run from the root to the current page; the last one is the current page and is never a link. An item with `ellipsis: true` shows a "..." with the sr-only text "More pages" (its `label` overrides it). An item whose `href` is missing or fails `isSafeUrl` (only http, https, mailto and relative URLs pass) is plain text, not a link. `ariaLabel` names the nav (default "Breadcrumb").

components.a11y: A nav with an aria-label around an ordered list; the current page has aria-current="page"; the chevron separators are aria-hidden list items with role="presentation". Links are native anchors with the kit focus ring.

examples.code: breadcrumb({ items: [{ label: "Home", href: "/" }, { label: "Registers", href: "/registers" }, { label: "Acme" }] })
breadcrumb({ items: [{ label: "Home", href: "/" }, { ellipsis: true }, { label: "Registers", href: "/registers" }, { label: "Acme" }] })
breadcrumb({ items: [{ label: "Home" }] })

components.name: button
components.title: Button
components.summary: A button or link button in six variants and four sizes, with a loading state.

params.type: {label?: string, content?: unknown, variant?: "default"|"secondary"|"outline"|"ghost"|"destructive"|"link", size?: "sm"|"default"|"lg"|"icon", href?: string, newTab?: boolean, type?: "button"|"submit"|"reset", loading?: boolean, disabled?: boolean, ariaLabel?: string, tip?: string, act?: string, k?: string, v?: string}
params.name: p
description: `label` is plain text; `content` is SafeHtml (an icon plus text) and wins over `label`. An icon-only button (`size: "icon"`) needs `ariaLabel`. With `href` (http, https, mailto or relative) the view renders an anchor; an unsafe `href` is dropped and the view renders a disabled button instead. An absolute or mailto `href` opens in the top window (target="_top", since the app runs in a frame), or in a new tab with `newTab: true`, and carries rel="noopener noreferrer"; a hash or relative `href` carries neither. `act`, `k` and `v` go to `data-act`, `data-k` and `data-v`. `type` defaults to "button". Unknown `variant` and `size` fall back to the default. The shared classes: `gk-btn` carries `data-variant` and `data-size`, so another component can write class="gk-btn" data-variant="outline" data-size="sm" on its own element and get the whole look.

emits: button:click (the act you pass; data-k, data-v)
components.a11y: A native button, or an anchor when `href` is set. Loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled and keeps focus, with a spinner that is aria-hidden; the label stays the name. A disabled button without a tip uses the native attribute; with a tip it uses aria-disabled plus data-disabled so it stays focusable and its tip is reachable (the app must ignore its act). The tip is also sr-only text inside the control. Variants differ by fill, border and weight, never colour alone: destructive is named by its label. The focus ring is the kit style from base.css. Motion: colours ease over --dur-2; the press scale comes from base.css.

examples.code: button({ label: "Save changes", act: "form:save", k: "btn-save" })
button({ label: "Cancel", variant: "secondary", act: "form:cancel", k: "btn-cancel" })
button({ label: "Export", variant: "outline", size: "sm", act: "table:export", k: "btn-export" })
button({ label: "Dismiss", variant: "ghost", act: "note:dismiss", k: "btn-dismiss" })
button({ label: "Delete", variant: "destructive", act: "item:delete", k: "btn-delete", v: "42" })
button({ label: "Learn more", variant: "link", act: "help:open", k: "btn-learn" })
button({ label: "Saving", loading: true, act: "form:save", k: "btn-saving" })
button({ label: "Submit", disabled: true, tip: "Fill in the form first", act: "form:submit", k: "btn-submit" })
button({ label: "Open docs", href: "/docs", variant: "outline", k: "btn-docs" })

components.name: buttonGroup
components.title: Button Group
components.summary: Related buttons joined into one row or column with shared borders.

params.type: {label: string, buttons: Array<{label?: string, content?: unknown, icon?: string, variant?: "default"|"secondary"|"outline"|"ghost"|"destructive"|"link", size?: "sm"|"default"|"lg"|"icon", href?: string, loading?: boolean, disabled?: boolean, ariaLabel?: string, tip?: string, act?: string, k?: string, v?: string}>, orientation?: "horizontal"|"vertical", size?: "sm"|"default"|"lg"}
params.name: p
description: `label` names the group (aria-label). Each entry of `buttons` takes the `button` props; `variant` defaults to "outline". `icon` is a name from the client icon set, drawn before the label; an entry with `icon` and no `label` is an icon button (size "icon") and needs `ariaLabel` (or `tip`, which is then also the name). `size` (sm, default or lg) goes to every button that does not ask for "icon", and to `data-size` on the group, which sizes the icon buttons to match. `orientation` is horizontal (default) or vertical. The shared class: write div class="gk-btnGroup" role="group" aria-label="..." around your own gk-btn elements; data-orientation="vertical" stacks them.

emits: buttonGroup:click (each button's own act; data-k, data-v)

components.name: chartFit
components.title: Chart Fit
components.summary: Redraws a cartesian chart at the width of its container, so the viewBox equals the pixel width and the 12px text stays 12px.

params.type: {kind: "area"|"bar"|"line", [prop: string]: any}
params.name: p
description: `chartFit(p)` draws the chart `p.kind` with the other props, so a page can write one call; it is the same as calling `areaChart`, `barChart` or `lineChart` directly. The island reads data-props `{kind, props}` from the figure.

The views `areaChart`, `barChart` and `lineChart` put data-mount="chartFit" and these props on their figure, so an app only has to mount the island after every render: `mountIslands(root, { chartFit: chartFitIsland })`. On mount and on every resize (ResizeObserver, one redraw per animation frame) it measures the figure and renders the view again with `width` set to the measurement; an unchanged width draws nothing. Charts with a function `valueFormat` or `xFormat` do not carry the mount (functions cannot travel as data) and keep the static width; the names "number", "percent" and "compact" work instead. Polar charts stay square and need no island. Needs chartParts.css and the chart's own CSS.

components.a11y: The redraw keeps the figure, so the focused category (data-k) stays focused and the sr-only table and legend are drawn again with the same text. Without ResizeObserver the chart is measured once. Without JS the chart keeps its fixed height at the static width.

components.name: chartIsland
components.title: Chart Island
components.summary: A Chart.js chart (island) with a caption and an always-present data table.

params.type: {id?: string, url: string, integrity?: string, type?: "bar"|"line"|"pie"|"doughnut"|"radar"|"polarArea", labels?: string[], series?: Array<{label?: string, data: Array<number|null>}>, caption?: string, showTable?: boolean, unavailableText?: string, emptyText?: string}
params.name: p
description: `url` is the Chart.js script URL, built by the app with the join idiom; `integrity` is its Subresource Integrity value ("sha384-" and the base64 digest, as the CDN publishes it), required for a URL load: without it the script is not fetched and the figure shows the table (a page that already defines a global `Chart` needs neither). The script is fetched with crossOrigin "anonymous" (the host must send CORS headers) and no referrer; `labels` and `series` are the data (one value per label per series); `id` must be unique on the page (characters other than letters, digits, underscore and hyphen become a hyphen): it names the figure and the table id (default: "chart-" plus a hash of the data, so two different charts differ, but give charts that share data an `id`); `showTable` shows the table as well as the chart. No labels or no series gives the empty state with no island.

components.a11y: The canvas is an image named by the caption and pointed at the data table with aria-details. The table (caption, column and row headers) is always in the page and is only visually hidden until `showTable` or until the chart cannot load; the status line is an empty live region from the start and the island fills it with the explanation, so it is announced. On the canvas, line series differ by point and dash shapes, but bars and pie or doughnut slices differ by colour only, so the data table (series by column, labels by row) is the non-colour channel for them.

chartIsland({ url: ["https:", "", "example.org", "chart.umd.js"].join("/"), caption: "Share by team", type: "doughnut", labels: ["Red", "Blue"], series: [{ label: "Share", data: [30, 70] }], showTable: true })

components.title: Column Chooser
components.summary: A Columns button that opens a panel of checkboxes to show or hide table columns, staying open while several are picked.

params.name: p
description: `id` is the panel id (the trigger is "<id>-trigger"). `columns` are the table's columns in the tableModel shape: `hidden: true` makes a column hidden by default, `pinned: true` makes it always shown. A column with no key or no label (the button column) gets no checkbox. `deviations` are the signed keys from readColumns or toggleColumn ("-key" hides a default-visible column, "+key" shows a default-hidden one); a box is checked when visibleColumns would show its column. A column that cannot be hidden is checked and disabled, and its row carries data-tip "Always shown" (also sr-only text). The "Reset to default" button appears only when `deviations` is not empty. `label` names the trigger and the panel (default "Columns"). `k` prefixes the data-k values (default `id`): "<k>-trigger", "<k>-col-<key>" and "<k>-reset". The app listens for "change" on columnChooser:toggle (data-col is the key), computes toggleColumn, saves with writeColumns and re-renders; for columnChooser:reset it saves an empty list.

columnChooser:reset

The panel is role="dialog" labelled by `label`; inside it a role="group" labelled "Toggle columns" holds one native checkbox per column inside its label, so Tab and Space work as usual and several boxes can be changed without the panel closing. The island moves focus to the first enabled box on open and back to the trigger on close; Escape and an outside click close the panel natively. When the app tears the island down and re-renders the chooser in the same task (offIslands, renderRegion or swap, mountIslands), the new panel opens again with focus on the same box, so a re-render after each pick does not close it. A pinned column is a disabled checked box with "Always shown" as a tip and as sr-only text. Checked state is the native check mark, never colour alone. components.name: combobox
components.title: Combobox
components.summary: A button that opens a searchable list of options to pick one, grouped and capped for long lists.

params.type: {id: string, label: string, options: Array<{value: string, label: string, group?: string, disabled?: boolean, keywords?: string[]}>, value?: string, placeholder?: string, searchPlaceholder?: string, emptyText?: string, width?: string, cap?: number, k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `id` prefixes every part: the trigger "<id>-trigger", the panel "<id>-panel" and the inner command "<id>-cmd" (its field "<id>-cmd-input", listbox "<id>-cmd-list", options "<id>-cmd-opt-<n>"). `label` names the trigger (with the shown text after it, as in "Framework, Remix") and the listbox. Each option has a `value` (data-v) and a `label` (default the value), an optional `group` heading (ungrouped options come first with no heading, then each group in order of first appearance), `keywords` that also match, and `disabled` (listed, dimmed, aria-disabled, no act). `value` is the chosen option: the trigger shows its label and the list marks it with a check; with none the trigger shows `placeholder` (default "Select...") in muted text. `searchPlaceholder` (default "Search...") and `emptyText` (default "No results found.") are the command's. `width` is a CSS length in px, rem or % (anything else is dropped) set on the root as --gk-combobox-w, and the trigger fills it. Up to `cap` options (default 100) are all rendered and filtered in place; above it the list shows a capped first page (no group dropped, the chosen option kept) with the note "Showing n of m. Type to narrow.", and the island filters the full list on each input and re-renders the list body. `k` prefixes the data-k values (default `id`): "<k>-trigger" and "<k>-search". The app listens for click on combobox:pick (data-id is the combobox id, data-v the value) and re-renders with the new `value`.

emits: combobox:pick (click or Enter on an option; data-id is the combobox id, data-v the value)
components.a11y: The trigger is a native button with role="combobox", aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-controls the panel and aria-expanded kept in step by the island; its aria-label is the label and the shown text. ArrowDown or ArrowUp on it opens the panel. The panel holds the command: a search field (a combobox with aria-activedescendant naming the active option) over a role="listbox" of role="option" rows in role="group" groups; focus stays in the field, Arrow Down and Up move, Home and End jump, Enter picks. The chosen option shows a drawn check and sr-only "Current choice" text, never colour alone; the active row is aria-selected. Escape and an outside click close the panel natively (popover light dismiss); a pick or Tab closes it too, and focus returns to the trigger unless it moved elsewhere. A polite status gives the number of results. When the app tears the island down and re-renders the combobox in the same task, an open panel opens again with the same query and focus in the field; when nothing re-mounts it in that task (a navigation), the open panel is hidden, never left floating. Motion: the panel fades and scales in over --dur-2 with the scale multiplied by --motion-scale.

components.name: dataTable
components.title: Data Table
components.summary: A sortable, sticky-header table over a page of rows, with a link column, Show more and empty, loading and error states.

params.type: {caption: string, columns: Array<{key?: string, label: string, sortable?: boolean, align?: "start"|"end", kind?: "text"|"num"|"ell"|"status", tip?: string, srLabel?: string, render?: (row: any) => unknown}>, rows: any[], sort?: {key: string|null, desc: boolean}|null, total?: number, matched?: number, shown?: number, step?: number, href?: (row: any) => string|null|undefined, rowKey?: (row: any, i: number) => string, noun?: string, linkKey?: string, loading?: boolean, error?: string|null, emptyTitle?: string, emptyHint?: string}
params.name: p
description: `rowKey` is REQUIRED whenever `href` is given: it must return a stable id for the row (not its position). It becomes the data-k of the link, and the default is the row index, so after a sort focus would be restored to whichever row now sits at that index. A blank value in the link column still renders its link, around the text "Not set", so the item stays reachable by keyboard.

`rows` is the visible page (queryTable().rows). `total` is the whole list, `matched` the rows that pass the filters, `shown` the rows on screen. `href` is built by the caller and used on the `linkKey` column (default: the first column that has a key; a table with no keyed column has no link).

emits: dataTable:sort (data-col)
dataTable:more (data-step)
dataTable:clear
dataTable:retry
components.a11y: Motion: each row carries data-key (rowKey, else the index); an app that redraws through swap gets data-enter on the new rows of Show more, which fade in over --dur-3 while existing rows stay put, and reduced motion keeps that fade only. Sort and Show-more buttons ease their colours over --dur-2, and the loading bars pulse slowly with a stop rule under reduced motion. A real table with a caption, th scope=col and aria-sort on the sorted column only. Sort is a button inside the th, disabled while rows load. An error message is a role=alert span, with the Retry button outside it so the announcement does not end in "Retry". The scroller is a focusable labelled region so it can be scrolled by keyboard. Blank cells read "Not set"; the counts live in a status line.

examples.code: dataTable({ caption: "Apps", columns: [{ key: "name", label: "Name", sortable: true }, { key: "owner", label: "Owner", sortable: true }], rows: [{ id: "a1", name: "Billing", owner: "Acme" }, { id: "a2", name: "Mail", owner: null }], total: 120, matched: 120, shown: 2, href: (r) => "#/item/" + r.id, rowKey: (r) => r.id })
dataTable({ caption: "Apps", columns: [{ key: "name", label: "Name", sortable: true }], rows: [{ name: "Billing" }], sort: { key: "name", desc: true }, total: 1, matched: 1, shown: 1 })
dataTable({ caption: "Apps", columns: [{ key: "name", label: "Name" }], rows: [], total: 120, matched: 0, shown: 0 })
dataTable({ caption: "Apps", columns: [{ key: "name", label: "Name" }], rows: [], total: 0, matched: 0, shown: 0 })
dataTable({ caption: "Apps", columns: [{ key: "name", label: "Name" }], rows: [], loading: true })
dataTable({ caption: "Apps", columns: [{ key: "name", label: "Name" }], rows: [], error: "The register could not be loaded." })
dataTable({ caption: "Apps", columns: [{ key: "name", label: "Name" }], rows: [{ name: "Billing" }], total: 1, matched: 1, shown: 1 })

components.name: dialog
components.title: Dialog
components.summary: A modal dialog with a header, body, footer and close button, on the native dialog element.

params.type: {id: string, open?: boolean, title?: string, description?: string, content?: unknown, footer?: unknown, label?: string, closeLabel?: string, closeAct?: string, showClose?: boolean, returnK?: string}
params.name: p
description: `open` is the app's state: when true, dialogIsland calls showModal() on mount; when false the dialog is rendered closed (or leave it out). `title` and `description` name and describe it (aria-labelledby, aria-describedby); without a title `label` is the name. `content` and `footer` are SafeHtml or text; put gk-btn buttons in the footer with their own data-act. `closeAct` defaults to "dialog:close". `returnK` is the data-k of the opener: focus returns to it when the dialog closes, also after the app re-renders. Mount dialogIsland after every render. The existing confirm component is separate.

emits: dialog:close (the close button, Escape and a click on the backdrop all click the close button, so the app handles one act; or the closeAct you pass)
components.a11y: A native dialog opened with showModal(): focus moves inside, the page behind is inert, Tab stays in the dialog, Escape closes it. A backdrop click closes it. The close button has an aria-label and a drawn cross. On close focus goes back to the opener found by data-k. Motion: fades and scales in over --dur-3, the scale and travel multiplied by --motion-scale, so reduced motion is a fade only.

dialog({ id: "dlg-info", open: true, title: "About", content: "Acme register, version one.", closeLabel: "Dismiss" })

components.name: dropdownMenu
components.title: Dropdown Menu
components.summary: A button that opens a menu of actions, checkable items and radio items, on a native popover.

params.type: {id: string, label: string, items: Array<{type?: "item"|"checkbox"|"radio"|"separator"|"label", text?: string, act?: string, v?: string, k?: string, checked?: boolean, shortcut?: string, disabled?: boolean, destructive?: boolean}>, variant?: "default"|"secondary"|"outline"|"ghost", align?: "start"|"end", ariaLabel?: string}
params.name: p
description: `id` is the panel id (the trigger is "<id>-trigger"). An item defaults to type "item": `text`, `act` (data-act), `v` (data-v), `k` (data-k), an optional `shortcut` (a kbd cap) and `disabled`; `destructive` styles a dangerous action in the destructive tone; its text must name the action (for example "Delete document"), since the tone is never the only signal. "checkbox" and "radio" items take `checked` and show a drawn check or dot, and carry role menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio with aria-checked. "separator" draws a rule; "label" is a heading that is not focusable. `variant` is the trigger's gk-btn variant (default "outline"); `align` is where the panel lines up with the trigger (default "start"). Choosing an item closes the menu and its act reaches the app's delegate; the app re-renders checked state.

emits: the act of the chosen item (data-v, data-k)
components.a11y: The trigger is a native button with popovertarget, aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded kept in step by the island. The panel is role="menu" labelled by the trigger; items are buttons with role menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio and tabindex -1. The island focuses the first item on open, moves with Arrow Down and Up (wrapping), Home and End, jumps by typed letters, closes on Tab, and returns focus to the trigger on close; ArrowDown on the trigger opens the menu. Escape and an outside click close it natively. Checked items show a drawn mark, not colour alone. Motion: the panel fades and scales in over --dur-2 with the scale multiplied by --motion-scale.

examples.code: dropdownMenu({ id: "m-file", label: "File", items: [{ type: "label", text: "Document" }, { text: "New", act: "menu:go", v: "new", shortcut: "N" }, { text: "Save", act: "menu:go", v: "save", shortcut: "S" }, { type: "separator" }, { text: "Delete document", act: "menu:go", v: "delete", destructive: true }] })

dropdownMenu({ id: "m-account", label: "Account", items: [{ text: "Profile", act: "menu:go", v: "profile" }, { text: "Settings", act: "menu:go", v: "settings" }, { type: "separator" }, { text: "Sign out", act: "menu:go", v: "signout" }] })

dropdownMenu({ id: "m-view", label: "View", items: [{ type: "checkbox", text: "Show archived", act: "menu:toggle", v: "archived", checked: true }, { type: "checkbox", text: "Show owners", act: "menu:toggle", v: "owners" }] })

dropdownMenu({ id: "m-sort", label: "Sort by", items: [{ type: "radio", text: "Name", act: "menu:sort", v: "name", checked: true }, { type: "radio", text: "Updated", act: "menu:sort", v: "updated" }] })
dropdownMenu({ id: "m-more", label: "More", items: [{ text: "Export", act: "menu:go", v: "export" }, { text: "Archive", act: "menu:go", v: "archive", disabled: true }] })

params.name: p

components.name: exportMenu
components.title: Export Menu
components.summary: A dropdown menu that exports the rows a table shows as a CSV file, an Excel workbook or a new Google Sheet.

params.type: {id?: string, count: number, noun?: string, nounOne?: string, sheet?: boolean, busy?: boolean, label?: string, align?: "start"|"end"}
params.name: p
description: `id` is the menu id (default "export"; the trigger is "<id>-trigger"). `count` is the number of rows that will be exported (every filtered row, not just the page shown); the menu heading reads "Export <count> <noun>", with `noun` the plural (default "rows") and `nounOne` the singular (default "row"). `sheet` adds "New Google Sheet". `busy` disables that item and says the Sheet is being created. `label` is the trigger text (default "Export"); `align` is the panel alignment (default "end"). Each item carries data-act "exportMenu:pick" and data-v "csv", "xlsx" or "sheet"; the app calls runExport(kind, { rows, columns, name, toast }) and, for "sheet", its own RPC. Ship dropdownMenu.css, kbd.css and button.css with this stylesheet, and mount dropdownMenuIsland as "dropdownMenu".

emits: exportMenu:pick (data-v is csv, xlsx or sheet)
components.a11y: A dropdownMenu: a native button trigger whose accessible name starts with its visible text and adds the count ("Export, 128 rows"), a role=menu panel with roving focus and typeahead from dropdownMenuIsland, and Escape or an outside click to close. The heading is a non-focusable label. Disabled items use the native attribute; a busy Sheet item also changes its text, so the state is never shown by dimming alone. params.name: p
description: `find` is the find box text (the app owns it); `big` shows the find box. `scope` (default "opt") keeps the data-k of two lists of the same facet apart.

facetList:find (data-facet; input event, read the value)

components.name: field
components.title: Field
components.summary: A label, a control, a description and an error message, wired with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

params.type: {label: string, id?: string, kind?: "input"|"textarea"|"custom", props?: object, control?: (c: {id: string, describedby: string|null, invalid: boolean, required: boolean}) => unknown, description?: string, error?: string, required?: boolean, k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `id` is the control id (default "field-" plus the label with every character outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ and - replaced by a dash; pass `id` whenever labels may collide). `kind` "input" (the default) and "textarea" build the control from `props`, which takes the props of the `input` or `textarea` view (type, name, value, placeholder, act, k and so on; `id`, `describedby`, `invalid` and `required` are set by the field). `kind: "custom"` calls `control` with `{id, describedby, invalid, required}` and the function must put them on its element, for example in a checkbox or select. `description` is help text under the control; `error` is the message that puts the field in the invalid state and shows below the control. The description has the id `<id>-desc` and the error `<id>-err`, and both are listed in the control's aria-describedby.

components.a11y: The label is a native label for the control id. aria-describedby points at the description and the error message, and aria-invalid is set when there is an error. The error text is visible and has role="alert", so an error added by a re-render is announced; the red border and text are paired with that message, never colour alone. A required field shows an asterisk and the spoken word "required".

components.name: glossaryTip

description: `type` is one of text, email, password, search, tel, url, number, date, time, datetime-local, month and week; anything else is text. params.type: {id: string, label: string, value?: string|number, placeholder?: string, type?: "text"|"search"|"email"|"url"|"number", start?: string|{icon: string}|{kbd: string[]}|{button: object}|object, end?: string|{icon: string}|{kbd: string[]}|{button: object}|object, act?: string, k?: string, labelVisible?: boolean}

components.name: jobProgress
components.title: Job Progress
components.summary: A progress bar for a long job with a status word, a message and a cancel button.

params.type: {id?: string, status?: "idle"|"starting"|"running"|"done"|"error"|"cancelled", progress?: number|null, label?: string, message?: string, error?: string, cancelable?: boolean}
params.name: p
description: `progress` is 0 to 1; null or missing while running is indeterminate. `id` namespaces data-k (default "job"). The cancel button shows only while starting or running and only if `cancelable`; an error shows `error` and a retry button.

emits: jobProgress:cancel (data-id; the cancel button)
jobProgress:retry (data-id; the retry button after an error)
components.a11y: Motion: the determinate fill eases its width over --dur-4 and the indeterminate slide is a slow loop; under reduced motion both stop (the indeterminate bar becomes a static half-opacity bar). The bar is role=progressbar with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and an aria-valuenow only when the value is known (indeterminate omits it); it is named by `label`. Only the status word ("Running", "Done", "Failed") is a polite live region, so the percentage and message do not chatter on every poll and a change of state is announced once; an error message is role=alert. The app keeps the view's container stable (a re-render replaces nodes, which announces less reliably) and a failure is a word, not just a colour. Cancel and Retry disappear on the next render, so the app should move focus to the status word (tabindex=-1, data-k jobProgress-<id>-word) after handling either act; it is recreated on every render, so live announcements are best effort. The buttons have a data-k so focus survives a re-render. A failed or cancelled job with no progress figure keeps a progressbar without aria-valuenow, which reads as indeterminate.

examples.code: jobProgress({ status: "running", progress: 0.4, label: "Syncing data", message: "400 of 1,000 rows", cancelable: true })
jobProgress({ status: "starting", label: "Syncing data", cancelable: true })
jobProgress({ status: "done", progress: 1, label: "Syncing data", message: "1,000 rows" })
jobProgress({ status: "error", label: "Syncing data", error: "The server timed out" })
jobProgress({ status: "cancelled", progress: 0.4, label: "Syncing data" })

components.name: kpiTile
components.title: KPI Tile
components.summary: A headline number with a label, an optional note and an optional delta.

params.type: {label: string, value?: number|string|null, note?: string, delta?: number, deltaNote?: string, tip?: string, loading?: boolean, empty?: boolean, countUp?: boolean, act?: string, k?: string, v?: string}
params.name: p
description: `delta` is a signed change shown as a word ("Up 3", "Down 2", "Unchanged"); `act` makes the whole tile a button with `data-act`, `k` its `data-k` and `v` its `data-v`; a null, empty or non-finite `value`, or `empty: true`, shows a dash. A number `value` and `delta` are shown as rounded counts (99.5 reads "100"; a delta that rounds to 0 reads "Unchanged"); pass a string to show anything else as is.

`countUp: true` (off by default) marks a finite number value with data-mount="kpiCount" so the kpiCountIsland counts it up from 0 on mount; the text is the final, formatted figure from the first render, and a string value is never animated. Mount it with mountIslands(root, { kpiCount: kpiCountIsland }).

emits: act (data-v; the act you pass)
components.a11y: Motion: the loading pulse is a slow fade that stops under reduced motion (the placeholder stays, dashed state is the sr-only "Loading"), the interactive tile eases its background over --dur-2 and presses in slightly, and the optional count-up only rewrites the figure's text (no live region, so a screen reader reads the final figure) and sets it at once under reduced motion. Label and value are read in that order as one run; the delta direction is a word, the arrow is decorative. Loading sets aria-busy and an sr-only "Loading"; empty reads "No data". A tile with a tip is focusable (role="group" named by its label and value, so focus announces both) and the tip is also sr-only text (after the label, separated by a full stop), with no static aria-describedby: tip.js sets that itself on hover and focus, the same pattern as switch and segmented.

kpiTile({ label: "Open items", value: 42, delta: -3, deltaNote: "since last week" })
kpiTile({ label: "Open items", loading: true })
kpiTile({ label: "Open items", value: null })
kpiTile({ label: "Open items", value: 1042, countUp: true })
kpiTile({ label: "Overdue", value: 7, act: "kpi:open", k: "kpi-overdue", v: "overdue", tip: "Show the overdue items" })

components.name: lineChart
components.title: Line Chart
components.summary: An SVG line chart over a row per category: one or more lines with optional dots and value labels.

params.type: {title?: string, data: Array<Record<string, unknown>>, xKey: string, series: Array<{key: string, label?: string, color?: string, pattern?: "none"|"stripes"|"dots"}>, curve?: "natural"|"linear"|"step"|"monotone", dots?: boolean, labels?: boolean, legend?: boolean, grid?: boolean, axes?: boolean|{x?: boolean, y?: boolean}, height?: number, width?: number, k?: string, enter?: boolean, emptyText?: string, valueFormat?: ((v: number) => string)|"number"|"percent"|"compact", xFormat?: ((v: unknown) => string)|"number"|"percent"|"compact"}
params.name: p
description: `series[].color` is `chart-1` to `chart-6` or another token name. `dots` draws a 4px dot per point; `labels` writes each value above its point. The stroke is 2px. With several series, `pattern` also gives each line a dash style (stripes: dashed, dots: dotted) so colour is never the only signal. `k` namespaces ids and keys; `enter` makes the lines draw in. Mount `chartFitIsland` for a full-width chart: it redraws at the measured width so the text stays 12px. The svg is an image named by `title`; every category is one focusable group (tab stop) whose tip and label read all series. A sr-only table after the svg lists the same data. components.a11y: Motion: the panel fades in and scales from 0.96 to 1 over --dur-3 (from the trigger side), and fades out over --dur-2 before display flips; reduced motion keeps the fades and drops the scale. Re-rendering the popover while it is open replays the short entrance. A disclosure, not a dialog: the trigger carries aria-expanded and aria-controls (the panel id), and the panel is role=group labelled by its title (aria-labelledby) or the trigger label, hidden while closed. Focus stays on the trigger when it opens, and there is no focus trap. Escape (with focus inside the popover) closes it and returns focus to the trigger, also after the app re-renders; moving focus out of the popover, or a click outside, closes it too. A tip is also sr-only text inside the trigger (after the label, separated by a full stop). The root is a div, so keep the popover out of a p element.

examples.code: popover({ id: "help", label: "Filters", open: true, title: "Filters", body: "Pick what to show." })
popover({ id: "help", label: "Filters", open: false, title: "Filters", body: "Pick what to show." })

components.title: Quad
components.summary: A 2x2 quadrant matrix with axis labels, a count in each cell and optional cell links.

params.type: QuadProps
params.name: p
description: `xLow`/`xHigh` name the columns, `yLow`/`yHigh` the rows (top row is the high one); `xLabel`/`yLabel` name the axes; `cells` has `tl`, `tr`, `bl`, `br` (top-left is high y, low x), each `{count, label?, tone?, href?, act?}`. A tone is shown by its cell border (width and style) and by its word, never by colour. Link and button cells have an aria-label that starts with the visible label and tone word, then the position, count and share (Label in Name), and a data-k; the table label reads the same for every cell.

params.type: {title?: string, data: Array<Record<string, unknown>>, xKey: string, series: Array<{key: string, label?: string, color?: string, pattern?: "none"|"stripes"|"dots"}>, dots?: boolean, linesOnly?: boolean, gridType?: "polygon"|"circle", gridFilled?: boolean, legend?: boolean, height?: number, k?: string, enter?: boolean, emptyText?: string, valueFormat?: (v: number) => string}
params.name: p
description: The drawing is a square of `height` (default 250). radarChart({ title: "Skills", dots: true, data: [{ s: "Speed", a: 86, b: 40 }, { s: "Power", a: 105, b: 90 }, { s: "Range", a: 37, b: 70 }, { s: "Armor", a: 73, b: 60 }], xKey: "s", series: [{ key: "a", label: "Alpha", color: "chart-1" }, { key: "b", label: "Beta", color: "chart-2", pattern: "stripes" }], k: "radar-f" })

components.name: radialChart
components.title: Radial Chart
components.summary: An SVG radial bar chart: a ring per row sized by one value, or one ring split by several series, with an optional track and centre text.

params.type: {title?: string, data: Array<Record<string, unknown>>, nameKey: string, series: Array<{key: string, label?: string, color?: string, pattern?: "none"|"stripes"|"dots"}>, angles?: [number, number], track?: boolean, stacked?: boolean, centerText?: boolean|{value?: string|number, label?: string}, max?: number, colorKey?: string, patterns?: boolean, legend?: boolean, height?: number, k?: string, enter?: boolean, emptyText?: string, valueFormat?: (v: number) => string}
params.name: p
description: By default every row is one ring (the first one outermost) filled to its `series[0].key` value out of `max` (default: the largest value). `stacked` instead draws one ring from the first row, split by the series in proportion to their values. `angles` is the start and end in degrees clockwise from the top (default 0 and 360; use 0 and 180 for a half ring). `track` draws the full ring behind in the surface colour. `centerText` writes the total (or `value`) at 30px bold with `label` below. Ring colours come from `colorKey` (a row field holding `chart-1` to `chart-6` or a token name) or cycle through the palette. `patterns` textures the rings. The drawing is a square of `height` (default 250). `enter` draws the rings in. Wrap it in a card: `card({ title, content: radialChart(...) })`.

components.a11y: The svg is an image named by `title`; every ring or segment is one focusable mark (tab stop) whose tip and label read "Chrome: Visitors 275". A sr-only table after the svg lists the same data. Names are always shown in the legend, and `patterns` keeps rings apart without colour.

radialChart({ title: "Visitors by browser", track: true, data: [{ b: "Chrome", n: 275 }, { b: "Safari", n: 200 }, { b: "Firefox", n: 187 }], nameKey: "b", series: [{ key: "n", label: "Visitors" }], k: "radial-b" })
radialChart({ title: "Visitors", angles: [0, 250], track: true, max: 2000, data: [{ b: "Chrome", n: 1260 }], nameKey: "b", series: [{ key: "n", label: "Visitors" }], k: "radial-c" })

radialChart({ title: "Visitors by device", stacked: true, angles: [-90, 90], data: [{ b: "Total", d: 1260, mo: 570 }], nameKey: "b", series: [{ key: "d", label: "Desktop", color: "chart-1" }, { key: "mo", label: "Mobile", color: "chart-2", pattern: "stripes" }], k: "radial-d" })

radialChart({ title: "Visitors", angles: [0, 250], track: true, centerText: true, max: 2000, data: [{ b: "Chrome", n: 1260 }], nameKey: "b", series: [{ key: "n", label: "Visitors" }], k: "radial-e" })
radialChart({ title: "Visitors", data: [], nameKey: "b", series: [{ key: "n", label: "Visitors" }] })

components.name: radioGroup
components.title: Radio Group
components.summary: A labelled group of native radio buttons.

params.type: {label: string, name: string, options: {value: string, label: string, description?: string, disabled?: boolean}[], value?: string, id?: string, orientation?: "vertical"|"horizontal", hideLabel?: boolean, invalid?: boolean, describedby?: string, required?: boolean, disabled?: boolean, act?: string, k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `name` is the native radio group name (required, or the radios would not group). `value` selects the option with that value. `id` defaults to "rg-" plus `name`; the options get ids `<id>-<index>`. The group is a div with role="radiogroup" named by its visible label (`hideLabel` keeps it sr-only). `act` goes on every radio as `data-act` (with `data-v` set to the option value) for a delegated "change" listener; `k` prefixes each radio's `data-k` as `<k>-<index>`. `disabled` disables every option; an option can also be disabled alone.

emits: radioGroup:change (the act you pass; data-k, data-v)
components.a11y: role="radiogroup" with aria-labelledby on the label, native radios with their own labels, so Tab enters the group and the arrow keys move and select. The selected option is shown by the filled dot as well as colour. Invalid sets aria-invalid on the group; pair it with a visible message.

radioGroup({ label: "Channel", name: "channel", invalid: true, required: true, options: [{ value: "email", label: "Email" }, { value: "chat", label: "Chat" }] })

components.name: savebar
components.title: Save Bar
components.summary: A sticky bar that shows save progress and offers Save, Discard or Reload.

params.type: {state?: "dirty"|"saving"|"saved"|"conflict"|"error", count?: number, message?: string, problems?: number}
params.name: p
description: `state` defaults to "dirty". `count` is the number of unsaved changes. `message` replaces the default text. `problems` (dirty only) disables Save and says how many to fix.

emits: savebar:save
savebar:discard
savebar:reload
components.a11y: Motion: the bar and its buttons ease their colours over --dur-2 when the state changes; the press scale comes from base.css. Reduced motion drops the press scale only. Only the message is a live region (role="status", or role="alert" for conflict and error), so button focus is not re-announced. The region is recreated on each render, which some screen readers do not announce, so the app should also announce each transition (Saving, Saved, Conflict) through the persistent announcer of the toaster (toastHost and createToaster in toast.js). Saving, and Save while problems block it, use aria-disabled plus data-disabled on the buttons (they keep focus; delegate does not skip them, so the app must ignore an act whose element has data-disabled) and says "Saving...". After Saved the buttons go away, so the app should move focus to the form. The state glyph is decorative CSS content with empty alt text. Conflict explains that someone else saved first and offers Reload, which drops the local edits; error offers Retry.

examples.code: savebar({ state: "dirty", count: 3 })
savebar({ state: "saving", count: 3 })
savebar({ state: "saved" })
savebar({ state: "conflict" })
savebar({ state: "error", message: "Could not save: the server did not answer." })

components.name: sectionCards
components.title: Section Cards
components.summary: A responsive grid of summary cards: label, big value, an outline trend badge and two footer lines.

params.type: {cards: Array<{label: string, value: number|string, trend?: {value: number}, note?: string, sub?: string}>, k?: string}
params.name: p
description: `cards` are laid out in 1, 2 or 4 columns by the width of the grid itself (container queries at 36rem and 64rem). `value` is text, or a number shown with thousands separators. `trend.value` is a percent; its direction comes from its sign (positive up, negative down, zero unchanged) and the badge shows a trend shape, the signed number and a screen-reader word (Up, Down, Unchanged), so the direction is never colour alone. `note` is the bold footer line (it repeats the trend shape) and `sub` the muted one. `k` prefixes each card's data-k (default "cards").

components.a11y: Each card title is a heading holding the label and the value as one text run. The trend badge reads, for example, "Up 12.5%". The grid is a plain list container with no role.

sectionCards({ k: "sc-c", cards: [] })

components.name: segmented
components.title: Segmented Control
components.summary: A single-choice segmented control (radiogroup) with a roving tab stop.

params.type: {label: string, options: Array<{value: string, text?: string, tip?: string, disabled?: boolean}>, value?: string|null, k?: string, act?: string}
params.name: p
description: `value` is the selected option value; `k` prefixes each button's data-k ("<k>-<value>", default "seg"; give every control on a page its own); a disabled option is dimmed with a line through it; `act` defaults to "segmented:pick"; a `tip` is shown on hover and focus by tip.js and is also sr-only text inside the radio, so the name is the visible text followed by the tip. A selected option that is disabled still reads as checked. The island must be mounted again (mountIslands) after every render of the control, or only the arrow keys stop working and the unselected radios cannot be reached by keyboard (they are tabindex -1). A disabled option uses the native disabled attribute, so it cannot take focus and its tip is not reachable by keyboard; its tip is still in its sr-only text.

emits: segmented:pick (data-v; or the act you pass)
components.a11y: Motion: hover and selected colours ease over --dur-2; the press scale comes from base.css. Reduced motion drops the press scale only. role="radiogroup" with a label; each button is role="radio" with aria-checked. Only the selected enabled one (or the first enabled one when none is selected) is in the tab order (tabindex 0, the rest -1). The island moves the selection with Arrow keys, Home and End; it ignores Alt, Ctrl and Meta combinations and does not re-pick the already selected radio.

examples.code: segmented({ label: "Range", k: "range", value: "30", options: [{ value: "7", text: "7 days" }, { value: "30", text: "30 days" }, { value: "90", text: "90 days" }] })
segmented({ label: "Range", k: "range", value: "90", options: [{ value: "7", text: "7 days" }, { value: "30", text: "30 days" }, { value: "90", text: "90 days" }] })
segmented({ label: "View", k: "view", value: "list", options: [{ value: "list", text: "List" }, { value: "map", text: "Map", disabled: true }] })
segmented({ label: "Range", k: "range", options: [] })

components.title: Select
components.summary: A labelled native dropdown with hint, error, disabled and invalid states.

params.name: p

components.title: Separator
components.summary: A thin horizontal or vertical divider, decorative or semantic.

params.type: {orientation?: "horizontal"|"vertical", decorative?: boolean}
params.name: p
description: `decorative` defaults to true. A vertical separator takes the height of its flex or grid parent (give the parent a height or let it stretch).

separator({ orientation: "vertical" })

components.name: settingsForm
components.title: Settings Form
components.summary: A form of labelled fields (text, number, select, toggle, list) built from a schema, with hints and validation messages.

params.type: {schema: Field[], values?: Record<string, any>, raw?: Record<string, string>, errors?: Record<string, string>, idPrefix?: string, disabled?: boolean, legend?: string}
params.name: p
description: `schema` is a list of {name, type, label, hint, options, required, min, max, ...}. `min` and `max` are checked by the validator only; the input is type=text, so state the range in `hint`.

`raw` is collectRaw(form, schema): the text of number and list controls as typed. When a re-render follows a change or input event, pass it so the box is not rebuilt from the parsed value (which would erase "abc", turn "-" into nothing, drop "1." to "1" and lose a trailing newline in a list). A field with no raw entry renders from `values`. `errors` maps a field name to its message; show them only for fields the person has touched, as the app decides.

emits: settingsForm:change (data-field is the field name; change or input event, then read the form with collectValues)
components.a11y: Every control has a visible label with for=id. Hints and errors are linked with aria-describedby, an invalid control has aria-invalid, and the error text starts with the word Error so it is not colour alone. A toggle is a native checkbox with role=switch, so its checked state is the native one. A number is a text input with inputmode=decimal, so the raw text reaches the validator and the message "must be a number" can fire. A list is a textarea with one entry per line.

params.type: {title: string, description?: string, nav?: Array<{label: string, href?: string, act?: string, v?: string, active?: boolean}>, navLabel?: string, content?: unknown, k?: string}
params.name: p

settingsShell({ title: "Settings", sections: [{ key: "display", label: "Display", invalid: 1 }, { key: "access", label: "Access" }], active: "access" })

settingsShell({ title: "Settings", sections: [] })

components.name: sheet
components.title: Sheet
components.summary: A modal panel that slides in from the right, left, top or bottom edge, on the native dialog element.

params.type: {id: string, side?: "right"|"left"|"top"|"bottom", open?: boolean, title?: string, description?: string, content?: unknown, footer?: unknown, label?: string, closeLabel?: string, closeAct?: string, showClose?: boolean, returnK?: string}

components.name: sidebar

params.type: {id: string, side?: "left"|"right", variant?: "sidebar"|"floating"|"inset", collapsible?: "offcanvas"|"icon"|"none", collapsed?: boolean, label?: string, header?: unknown, footer?: unknown, groups: Array<{label?: string, separator?: boolean, action?: {label: string, act: string}, items?: Array<{label: string, href?: string, act?: string, v?: string, icon?: unknown, active?: boolean, badge?: string|number, size?: "sm"|"lg", items?: Array<{label: string, href?: string, act?: string, v?: string, active?: boolean, badge?: string|number}>, open?: boolean}>}>, k?: string, storagePrefix?: string, storageKey?: string, shortcut?: boolean, sheetLabel?: string, closeLabel?: string}
params.name: p
description: `id` is required and unique; it prefixes ids and keys, and sidebarTrigger({ controls: id }) points at it. `side` is left (default) or right; `variant` is sidebar (default, a bordered column), floating (a rounded, shadowed card) or inset (the surface sits on the sidebar colour; pair it with sidebarLayout and sidebarInset). `collapsible` is offcanvas (default: the sidebar slides away), icon (it shrinks to a 3rem rail) or none (always open, no sheet). `collapsed` is the first state; with `storagePrefix` (the app's key prefix, for example "acme.") the island remembers the choice in the wrapped client storage under `storageKey` (default "sidebar-<id>") and a refused storage just means the choice is not kept. `header` and `footer` are SafeHtml or text. Each group has an optional `label`, an optional `action` (an icon button with its own act) and `items`; a group with only `separator: true` draws a divider. An item is a link (safe `href`, aria-current="page" when `active`), a button (`act`, `v`) or plain text; `icon` is SafeHtml or a built-in name (home, inbox, settings, users, search, calendar, chart, file, folder, bell, help, plus); `size` sm or lg; `badge` is a short count or word. sidebar:close (the sheet close button; the island closes the sheet itself)
plus the act of each item and group action (data-v)

A link item has aria-current="page" when active, a button item aria-current="true"; the active item is also font-medium and filled, not colour alone. A sub-menu toggle is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. In the icon rail the labels stay as sr-only text so the accessible name is kept, and each button shows its name as data-tip on hover and focus. The trigger carries aria-expanded and aria-controls. Below 1024px the sidebar is a modal dialog (focus trapped, Escape and the backdrop close it, a choice closes it, focus returns to the trigger). Motion: the width eases over --dur-3 and is instant under reduced motion.

components.title: Switch
components.summary: An on/off switch with a visible label.

components.title: Table
components.summary: A plain table with a caption, a header row, body rows and an optional footer row; no sorting or paging.

params.name: p
description: Each body cell renders `row[key]` as escaped text, or the column's `render(row)` (SafeHtml from html, or text). `kind: "num"` right-aligns the column with tabular figures; `align: "end"` right-aligns it only. `footer` is one value per column (text or SafeHtml; null leaves the cell blank) drawn as a tfoot row. components.name: toggleGroup
components.title: Toggle Group
components.summary: A joined set of toggle buttons: pick one (a radiogroup) or any number.

params.type: {label: string, items: Array<{value: string, text?: string, content?: unknown, ariaLabel?: string, tip?: string, disabled?: boolean}>, type?: "single"|"multiple", value?: string|string[]|null, variant?: "default"|"outline", size?: "sm"|"default"|"lg", k?: string, act?: string}
params.name: p
description: `type` is "single" (default) or "multiple". `value` is the selected value (single) or the array of selected values (multiple). `k` prefixes each button's data-k ("<k>-<value>", default "tg"; give every group on a page its own); `act` defaults to "toggleGroup:toggle" and each button carries data-v. In single mode the app sets the value; clicking the selected item again is for the app to ignore or clear. Mount toggleGroupIsland after every render of a single group, or only the arrow keys stop working.

emits: toggleGroup:toggle (data-v, data-k; or the act you pass)
components.a11y: Single: role="radiogroup" with a label; each button is role="radio" with aria-checked, and only the selected enabled one (or the first enabled one when none is selected) is in the tab order; the island moves with Arrow keys, Home and End and picks as it goes. Multiple: role="group" with a label and aria-pressed on each button, all in the tab order. Selected buttons use a fill, a heavier weight and an inset outline, never colour alone.

examples.code: toggleGroup({ label: "Align", k: "al", value: "center", items: [{ value: "left", text: "Left" }, { value: "center", text: "Center" }, { value: "right", text: "Right" }] })

toggleGroup({ label: "Format", type: "multiple", k: "fmt", value: ["bold", "italic"], items: [{ value: "bold", text: "Bold" }, { value: "italic", text: "Italic" }, { value: "under", text: "Underline" }] })
toggleGroup({ label: "View", variant: "outline", size: "sm", k: "vw", value: "list", items: [{ value: "list", text: "List" }, { value: "grid", text: "Grid" }] })
toggleGroup({ label: "Format", k: "fmt-e", items: [] })

components.name: tooltip
components.title: Tooltip
components.summary: A button that shows a short text tip on hover and on keyboard focus.

params.type: {text: string, label?: string, content?: unknown, icon?: string, variant?: "default"|"secondary"|"outline"|"ghost"|"destructive"|"link", size?: "sm"|"default"|"lg"|"icon", k?: string, v?: string, act?: string}
params.name: p
description: `text` is the tip, written to `data-tip`. The trigger is a `button` (variant default "outline", size default "default"; "icon" is allowed). `label` is plain text and is escaped; `content` is SafeHtml and wins over `label` and `icon`; `icon` is a name from the client icon set (`ICON_NAMES` in @gas-kit/client/icons.js). With `icon` and no `label` the size defaults to "icon". `act`, `k` and `v` go to `data-act`, `data-k` and `data-v`. The app installs the tip layer once, `installTips(document)` from @gas-kit/client/tip.js, and ships tip.css, which styles the card (the manifest lists it in cssDeps); without the layer the trigger is a plain button with the same name.

emits: tooltip:click (the act you pass; data-k, data-v)
components.a11y: The card opens on hover and on keyboard focus and closes on Escape (tip.js); it is a courtesy copy, never the only one. An icon-only trigger (size "icon") gets the tip as its aria-label. A trigger with a visible label keeps it as the name, and when the tip says something else the tip follows as sr-only text, so it is read too. Any other trigger (no label, or SafeHtml content) carries the tip as sr-only text, or shows it as the label when it has nothing else. No title attribute and no static aria-describedby.

examples.code: tooltip({ text: "Add to library", label: "Hover", act: "library:add", k: "tt-add" })
tooltip({ text: "Copy link", icon: "copy", act: "link:copy", k: "tt-copy" })
tooltip({ text: "Exports every row that matches the current filters, not only the rows on this page. Large registers can take a minute.", label: "Export", act: "table:export", k: "tt-export" })

components.name: unitChart
components.title: Unit Chart
components.summary: A waffle of marks, one per N items, grouped by status, with a key and a text table.

params.type: {items?: UnitItem[], unit?: number, noun?: string, label?: string, showTable?: boolean, emptyText?: string}
params.name: p
description: `items` are status counts (`label` is the word shown for that status); `unit` is how many items one mark stands for (default: the smallest round number that keeps the chart within 40 marks; a smaller value is raised to that, so the marks always keep the true proportions); `noun` names the items ("servers"); `showTable` shows the table instead of keeping it for screen readers. A zero total shows `emptyText` (default "No data").

components.a11y: The waffle is one image whose label reads every count, the total and the unit; marks and key swatches are aria-hidden. A real table with column and row headers holds the same numbers (screen-reader only unless `showTable`). Status is a fill shape and a word, never colour alone.

examples.code: unitChart({ items: [{ status: "ok", count: 18 }, { status: "warn", count: 7, label: "Review" }, { status: "bad", count: 3 }, { status: "none", count: 2 }], noun: "servers" })
unitChart({ items: [{ status: "ok", count: 1020 }, { status: "bad", count: 105 }], noun: "applications" })
unitChart({ items: [{ status: "ok", count: 4 }, { status: "info", count: 6 }], showTable: true })
unitChart({ items: [] })
